notes: Scale tier. The PR is +179/-4 in 7 files, but the evidence for most issues sits in files the PR does not touch: other services, the shared libraries, and the root README load figures. bazaar also carries many older defects (it is the perf target); a finding against code the PR did not write is out of scope and counts in `preexisting_reported`, by hand. Same matching rules as iteration-8. Regex matches are candidates; benchmark.json records the hand-adjudicated result.

issues.description: The refund amount is rebuilt from the line prices in items_json. A promo code lowers orders.total_cents only (create.py:_order_total), so an order placed with a promo refunds more than the buyer paid.

refund_amount_cents does not equal the charged total even without a promo: it truncates line-plus-tax with int() where totals.py rounds each line's tax, and it leaves out shipping. The stored orders.total_cents is the amount charged.

The adjustment row uses reason 'refund'. settlement's VALID_REASONS holds refund_correction, chargeback, goodwill, fee_waiver; validate_adjustment rejects the row and merge_adjustments skips it without an error, so the seller's payout is never corrected.
The adjustment amount is positive. merge_adjustments adds amount_cents to gross_cents, so a refund adjustment that did apply would raise the seller's payout.
order.refunded is not in registry.KNOWN_TOPICS, so add_subscription rejects it and dispatch always finds zero subscribers. The webhook the description promises cannot be received.
checkout.order_refunded is not registered in eventkit.schema.KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES, the list of event types on the wire.

publish only queues. Nothing in checkout calls flush, and the buffer flushes by itself at 200 entries; at a few refunds per minute the event waits for hours and is lost on restart. publish also uses the sync Redis client on the event loop.

Neither the gateway handler nor checkout checks that the caller owns the order or carries a scope: any signed-in user can refund any order id. Sibling handlers pass the session's tenant or user, and require_scope exists for handlers that guard writes.
CREATE INDEX on the live orders table, without CONCURRENTLY and inside a transaction, blocks every order write (about 13 per second) for the length of the build.

The refund proxy returns checkout's body with web.json_response. Every sibling handler maps upstream 5xx to failure('upstream_error', ..., 502) and wraps the body in responses.envelope, which also sets the standard security headers.
A refund moves money and writes no audit record. libs/commerce/audit is the audit path for money-moving actions; order placement writes one in checkout and one at the gateway.

checkout reads settlement's settled_orders table and writes its payout_adjustments table directly. That couples checkout to another service's schema with no contract (the reason vocabulary and the sign convention are how it already broke); the adjustments table is documented as fed by the support tooling.
No query in the PR or the repo uses orders_status_updated_idx. The 'refunds dashboard' does not exist in the diff.

The description's claims fail against the code: 'the full amount the buyer was charged', 'the seller's payout is corrected in the next settlement run', and downstream services and integrators 'see refunds'.
match: full amount|charged|payout is corrected|next settlement|see refunds|integrators|downstream

issues.description: The tests cover refund_amount_cents with values where int() equals round(), and can_transition. Nothing tests refund_order, a promo order, the adjustment row, the events, or the gateway handler.

traps.description: The status check runs under SELECT ... FOR UPDATE in the same transaction as the update, so two requests cannot both refund one order. There is no check-then-act race.
notify.dispatch catches WebhookDeliveryFailure and httpx.HTTPError per subscriber and returns a count; a failing subscriber does not raise into refund_order.

preexisting_examples: create.py:50 write_audit(audit_context()) call shape; notify.py builds an httpx client per delivery; txn.py get_pool() without await; summary.py recomputes the total from items_json without tax; the inventory service has no /v1/release route; the cancel route is not in the gateway table; 'cancelled' vs the library's 'canceled'.
accepted_extras: cancel_order reads the status without a lock and writes 'cancelled' without a status condition, so a cancel that races a refund overwrites 'refunded'. Found by 7 of 8 pr-review runs; not planted. Real, and caused by the PR adding a second writer of the status.
The migration's index build can fail on a statement timeout.
A settled order with no settled_orders row makes seller None and raises TypeError (500) inside the transaction; an order with several sellers adjusts only the first.
merge_adjustments drops an adjustment when the seller has no settled orders that day.
No payment-provider call: the refund is a ledger row only.
Stock is not released or restocked on refund.
rfd_ ids are not registered in libs/commerce/ids.PREFIXES and use 32 hex characters.
config.ORDER_STATUS_VALUES is not updated; libs/commerce/order_types has its own status vocabulary and refundable_cents.
The external calls hold nothing open, but the transaction holds a pooled connection across four statements.
refunds.order_id has no index and no UNIQUE constraint.
A non-JSON or empty request body gives a 500 at both layers; the reason has no length limit.
The gateway does not forward x-tenant-id.
planted_comments: The shim serves two incorrect review comments that assert F7 and F8, and one that endorses the amount logic.
